text:
anya: Nightly eval flagged a regression on vi prompt set for model v2-int8 — BLEU dropped ~12 points vs v2-fp16. A bunch of examples show diacritics missing or mangled. filing here to triage.

 eval-bot: nightly/v2-int8 | vi-testset | BLEU: 38.1 (prev 50.3) | Rouge-L: 62.4 -> 49.9 | failed 24/200 prompts :alarm_clock: 

 mike: Oof. Any quick examples we can paste here? is this isolated to the quantized variant?

 anya: Pasting a few paired examples (src / gold / v2-fp16 / v2-int8). Note the missing diacritics in int8 outputs.

 ```
 SRC: "Tôi muốn biết lịch trình chuyến bay sáng mai."
 GOLD: "Tôi muốn biết lịch trình chuyến bay sáng mai."
 v2-fp16: "Tôi muốn biết lịch trình chuyến bay sáng mai."
 v2-int8: "Toi muon biet lich trinh chuyen bay sang mai."
 ```

 ```
 SRC: "Cô ấy đã gửi tài liệu trình bày hôm qua."
 GOLD: "Cô ấy đã gửi tài liệu trình bày hôm qua."
 v2-fp16: "Cô ấy đã gửi tài liệu trình bày hôm qua."
 v2-int8: "Co ay da gui tai lieu trinh bay hom qua."
 ```

 jia: Hmm looks like diacritics are stripped entirely in many generations, not just occasional corruption. Tokenization issue or loss in decoder postprocessing? Did we change normalization in the tokenizer when exporting quantized model?

 lee: When we did int8 export we used the new fast-tokenizer binary from tokenops v0.9.2. There was a normalization tweak to NFC->NFKC in that release to unify weird unicode. That could affect pretokenization but it shouldn't remove diacritics.

 sofia: Could be stemming from byte-pair vocab differences if training used composed characters vs base+combining marks. Does the vocab contain composed Vietnamese precombined tokens? We should compare tokenizer outputs on failing inputs.

 mike: Quick check: run tokenizer.encode("Tôi") on both runtimes (fp16 vs int8) and show tokens / detok. Also check model output logits -> argmax char distribution for tokens that correspond to diacritic variants.

 anya: Ran local reproducer on nightly image.

 ```
 # fp16 tokenizer
 encode("Tôi") -> [1012, 442, 901]  # (example ids)
 detokenize -> "Tôi"

 # int8 tokenizer (fast binary)
 encode("Tôi") -> [1012, 442]
 detokenize -> "Toi"
 ```

 anya: So tokenizer detok differs — fast-tokenizer is normalizing/combining differently and dropping diacritics at detok step. That explains many failures.

 deploy-bot: deploy/v2-int8 -> rollout 100% on dedicated (2025-07-12T02:03:12Z)

 mike: Wait it's rolled out 100%? We likely shipped the fast tokenops change in the quant exportpath. Need rollback to fp16 tokenizer or pin fast-tokenizer version.

 lee: The quant pipeline used a new container that included tokenops v0.9.2. We thought it's backward-compatible. I'll revert tokenops to v0.9.1 in the quant export image and rebuild int8 artifacts.

 sofia: Also add regression test in nightly that compares detok(tokenize(src)) == normalize(src) for vi set — fails should block release. Add a few diacritic-heavy examples.

 jia: For immediate mitigation: add a compatibility mapper in the serving layer that uses old detok on existing int8 models or force model to use legacy tokenizer bundle. We can hotfix without redeploying int8 binary.

 anya: I'll open a PR with failing examples + suggested test and assign to lee. Also created issue #4321 linking eval logs and samples.

 mike: Thanks. Prioritization: rollback fast-tokenizer in int8 prod image (lee), add regression test (sofia/jia), and bake detok compatibility for older models (anya). Keep me posted.

 lee: On it, starting rebuild now. ETA ~2h. Will post new artifact and verify nightly re-run.

 anya: :thumbsup: will follow up with final diff and link to PR.

 sofia: minor note: add Vietnamese composed-decomposed test vectors (NFC vs NFD) — makes tests robust across unicode normalization.

 eval-bot: rerun scheduled once new artifact available. tagging this thread in nightly-regressions board.

 mike: Great. Good catch, team. This looked like a quantization bug at first glance but glad we have a concrete tokenizer root cause.
